# vendor

- `commonware-storage/`: commonware-storage 2026.9.0 exactly as published on crates.io (`commonware-storage-2026.9.0.crate`, sha256 `15ec50ba1efad76170c65d8c53baefc49da20eed02df9eedb3aa0754f2ff1d53`, the checksum `Cargo.lock` pinned), built in its place through `[patch.crates-io]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Patched on top of it, in its own commit: an owned reader of an Any QMDB's operation log (`qmdb::any::db::Db::reader`, `journal::authenticated::Reader`, `merkle::full::Reader`, `journal::contiguous::Snapshottable`, and `qmdb::sync::Source` for the reader), so the node serves `/v1/sync` from what its block writer publishes. The existing `qmdb::sync::Journal` trait is publicly re-exported so state sync can receive raw operations into its resumable journal and call `Database::from_sync_result` without using the proof-fetch engine. `journal::authenticated::Reader::historical_range_proof` (the proof half of its `historical_proof`) and a public `qmdb::inactive_peaks_at` let the node prove exactly the operations one `/v1/sync` answer read within its byte and time bounds. Recovery, journal bytes and database construction are unchanged. The copy and its `[patch.crates-io]` line go at the first commonware release that carries an equivalent reader; no upstream PR is filed.
